label: PARITY (official reference code run; bit-exact, abs_diff=0.0, incl. real ill-conditioned layer clouds)
paper: Razzhigaev, Mikhalchuk, Goncharova, Gerasimenko, Oseledets, Dimitrov, Kuznetsov (2024). 'Your Transformer is Secretly Linear.' ACL 2024 (long), arXiv:2405.12250.

reference_impl.transform: UNCONSTRAINED least-squares linear map A = X^+ Y via thin-SVD pseudo-inverse (NOT orthogonal Procrustes A=UV^T)
reference_impl.pipeline: center columns -> Frobenius-normalize (x/x.norm()) -> A = Vh^T diag(1/S) U^T Y -> sim = 1 - ||X A - Y||_F^2 (||Y||_F=1 after normalization)

blme_port_note: BLME runs the SAME torch.linalg.svd + unguarded 1/S as the reference (promoted to float64 for determinism), NOT numpy. This is required: on ill-conditioned clouds numpy's and torch's SVD resolve the ~1e-17 null-space singular values differently and the unguarded 1/S amplifies them by ~1e17, so a numpy port would disagree with the reference by up to ~0.4. Using torch => bit-exact (abs_diff 0.0) on both toys AND real layer clouds. BLME adds one guard only: NaN on a degenerate constant / exactly-singular cloud where the reference emits NaN/inf.

anchor_orthogonal.desc: Y = X @ Q, Q random ORTHOGONAL (proper Procrustes rotation) => Y in row space of X => sim == 1.0

anchor_independent.desc: Y independent random Gaussian => low linearity (~0.08, well below 1)

anchor_scaled_2x.desc: Y = 2*X. Frobenius-normalization removes the global scale, so the identity map sends normalized X exactly onto normalized Y => sim == 1.0. Documents that the score is scale-invariant.

anchor_wide_NleD.desc: N<D (12x40), full row-rank X, Y=X@A exactly in row space. Now bit-exact vs the reference because BLME uses the same torch SVD. (An earlier numpy port gave 1.0 here vs the reference's ~0.996 — a null-space-resolution artifact, now eliminated.)

conditioning_caveat.desc: When X is near-rank-deficient (effective rank << D), the value is dominated by how the SVD backend resolves ~1e-17 singular values, which the unguarded 1/S amplifies by ~1e17. numpy vs torch SVD then disagree by up to ~0.4 on the SAME input, and a numerically-stable solver returns ~1.0 (Y truly in X's column space). The reference is DEFINED by torch, so BLME uses torch and reproduces it bit-exactly; but the absolute value is a conditioning artifact, not a robust linearity. The metric is well-posed only for reasonably-conditioned X (paper toy is (1000,10)). Interpret the across-depth PROFILE, not a single absolute value.
conditioning_caveat.example_pythia70m: on real pythia-70m clouds (N~987, D=512), numpy port gave 1.0 for every pair while torch reference gave 0.92-0.99; BLME (torch) matches the reference bit-exactly.
